title: Youthful Sour Saudi Arabian Saskatoon Berries Tagine
description: A sweet and sour Saudi Arabian dish featuring Saskatoon berries, perfect for a lazy Sunday, with a unique ice-bath-shock step to preserve the berries' texture. This recipe is onion and garlic free, making it suitable for those with dietary restrictions.
instructions: Rinse the Saskatoon berries and pick out any stems or debris.
In a large bowl, mix together the lemon juice, apple cider vinegar, and honey until well combined.
Add the Saskatoon berries to the bowl and toss to coat with the lemon mixture.
Let the berries sit at room temperature for 30 minutes to allow them to release their juice.
In a small bowl, whisk together the water and cornstarch until smooth.
Add the cornstarch mixture to the bowl with the berries and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove the bowl from the heat and stir in the salt, black pepper, and cardamom powder.
Immediately submerge the bowl in an ice bath to stop the cooking process and preserve the texture of the berries.
Let the tagine cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until chilled.
Serve the tagine cold, garnished with additional Saskatoon berries if desired.
